candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a least common denominator (LCD) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks define the same operation: compute an LCD/LCM for denominators and convert to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions once denominators match by subtracting numerators and keeping the common denominator (including within mixed-number subtraction).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A/B/C each describe performing the actual fraction subtraction after alignment (like denominators), typically as numerator subtraction over the common denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite or regroup whole and fractional parts (including borrowing 1 as b/b, rewriting a whole number as a mixed number, or converting mixed to improper) to make subtraction possible when the fractional part would be negative or to set up the subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three include restructuring/regrouping between whole and fractional parts; B’s version explicitly includes mixed↔improper conversion as setup, which is also included in C and is not excluded by A (A excludes only cases where conversion occurs without any regrouping/borrowing).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the final fraction to lowest terms and express the final answer in an appropriate form (integer, proper fraction, or mixed number).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C match directly on final simplification/formatting; B combines regrouping-with-simplification in one skill, but it clearly includes the same final-step simplification and final-form expression component.

alignment_summary: Across the three expert codebooks, four shared skill concepts align cleanly: (1) converting to a common denominator, (2) subtracting fractions with aligned denominators, (3) regrouping/restructuring mixed numbers to enable subtraction (including borrowing and sometimes mixed↔improper conversion as setup), and (4) simplifying and expressing the final result. All skills from A, B, and C map to these four concepts with full 3/3 consensus.
